*Leader:* May my praise be a crown for Your head, and like incense before You, the prayers I have said.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/29)

*Cong:* May a poor man’s song be precious in Your eyes, like a song sung over sacrifice.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 30

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/30](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/30)

*Leader:* To the One who sustains all, may my blessing take flight: Creator, Life-Giver, God of right and might.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 31

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/31](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/31)


*קהל:* וּבְבִרְכָתִי תְנַעֲנַע לִי רֹאשׁ, וְאוֹתָהּ קַח לְךָ כִּבְשָׂמִים רֹאשׁ.


*Cong:* And when I offer blessing, to me Your head incline: accepting it as spice, fragrant and fine.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 32

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/32](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/32)


*ש״ץ:* יֶעֱרַב נָא שִׂיחִי עָלֶֽיךָ, כִּי נַפְשִׁי תַעֲרֹג אֵלֶֽיךָ.


*Leader:* May my prayer be to You sweet song. For You my soul will always long.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 34

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/34](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/34)


לְךָ יהוה הַגְּדֻלָּה וְהַגְּבוּרָה וְהַתִּפְאֶֽרֶת וְהַנֵּֽצַח וְהַהוֹד, כִּי־כֹל בַּשָּׁמַֽיִם וּבָאָֽרֶץ, לְךָ יהוה הַמַּמְלָכָה וְהַמִּתְנַשֵּׂא לְכֹל לְרֹאשׁ׃ מִי יְמַלֵּל גְּבוּרוֹת יהוה, יַשְׁמִֽיעַ כָּל־תְּהִלָּתוֹ׃


Yours, LORD, are the greatness and the power, the glory, the majesty and splendor, for everything in heaven and earth is Yours. Yours, LORD, is the kingdom; You are exalted as ead over all. Who can tell of the mighty acts of the LORD and make all His praise be heard?

**קדיש יתום**


**MOURNER’S KADDISH**


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 37

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/37](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/37)


*אבל:* יִתְגַּדַּל וְיִתְקַדַּשׁ שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא (*קהל:* אָמֵן)
בְּעָלְמָא דִּי בְרָא כִרְעוּתֵהּ
וְיַמְלִיךְ מַלְכוּתֵהּ
בְּחַיֵּיכוֹן וּבְיוֹמֵיכוֹן וּבְחַיֵּי דְּכָל בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
בַּעֲגָלָא וּבִזְמַן קָרִיב, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן. (*קהל:* אָמֵן)


*Mourner:* יִתְגַּדַּל Magnified and sanctified
may His great name be,
in the world He created by His will.
May He establish His kingdom
in your lifetime and in your days,
and in the lifetime
of all the house of Israel,
swiftly and soon – and say: Amen.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 38

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/38](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/38)


*קהל ואבל:* יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא.


*All:* May His great name be blessed for ever and all time.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 39

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/39](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/39)


*אבל:* יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח וְיִתְפָּאַר וְיִתְרוֹמַם וְיִתְנַשֵּׂא
וְיִתְהַדָּר וְיִתְעַלֶּה וְיִתְהַלָּל
שְׁמֵהּ דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא (*קהל:* בְּרִיךְ הוּא)
לְעֵֽלָּא לְעֵֽלָּא מִכָּל בִּרְכָתָא וְשִׁירָתָא, תֻּשְׁבְּחָתָא וְנֶחֱמָתָא
דַּאֲמִירָן בְּעָלְמָא, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן. (*קהל:* אָמֵן)


*Mourner:* Blessed and praised, glorified and exalted,
raised and honored, uplifted and lauded
be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He,
above and beyond any blessing,
song, praise and consolation
uttered in the world – and say: Amen.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 40

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/40](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/40)


יְהֵא שְׁלָמָא רַבָּא מִן שְׁמַיָּא
וְחַיִּים, עָלֵֽינוּ וְעַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן. (*קהל:* אָמֵן)


May there be great peace from heaven,
and life for us and all Israel – and say: Amen.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Shir HaKavod 42

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/42](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Shir%20HaKavod/r/42)


עֹשֶׂה הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו
הוּא יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם עָלֵֽינוּ וְעַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן. (*קהל:* אָמֵן)


May He who makes peace in His high places,
make peace for us and all Israel – and say: Amen.



### Massekhet Yoma


#### Chapter

###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:1)


שִׁבְעַת יָמִים קֹדֶם יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
מַפְרִישִׁין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מִבֵּיתוֹ לְלִשְׁכַּת פַּלְהֶדְרִין
וּמַתְקִינִין לוֹ כֹהֵן אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו
שֶׁמָּא יֶאֱרַע בּוֹ פְסוּל.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
אַף אִשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת מַתְקִינִין לו
שֶׁמָּא תָמוּת אִשְׁתּוֹ
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְכִפֶּר בַּעֲדוֹ וּבְעַד בֵּיתוֹ:
בֵּיתוֹ – זוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ.
אָמְרוּ לוֹ:
אִם כֵּן, אֵין לַדָּבָר סוֹף.


1 Seven days before the Day of Atonement,
the High Priest is brought away from his house
and taken to the Chamber of Palhedrin,
and another priest is appointed as his substitute,
in case something should happen to disqualify him.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Another wife is appointed to him also,
in case his wife should die –
for it is written, “He shall make atonement for himself and for his house”:
*his house* means “his wife.”
The sages say:
But if so, there would be no end to it.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:2)


כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים
הוּא זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם
וּמַקְטִיר אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת
וּמֵטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת
וּמַקְרִיב אֶת הָרֹאשׁ וְאֶת הָרֶגֶל;
וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַיָּמִים
אִם רָצָה לְהַקְרִיב – מַקְרִיב
שֶׁכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מַקְרִיב חֵלֶק בָּרֹאשׁ
וְנוֹטֵל חֵלֶק בָּרֹאשׁ.


2 All the seven days beforehand,
he throws the blood [of the daily sacrifices],
burns the incense,
tends the lamps,
and offers up the head and the right hind leg [of the daily sacrifice].
On other days [of the year],
if he wants to perform any offering, he does,
for the High Priest always has first choice to make the offering,
and the first choice of portion to take [from the offering].


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:3)


מָסְרוּ לוֹ זְקֵנִים מִזִּקְנֵי בֵית דִּין
וְקוֹרִין לְפָנָיו בְּסֵדֶר הַיּוֹם
וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ: אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, קְרָא אַתָּה בְּפִיךָ
שֶׁמָּא שָׁכַחְתָּ אוֹ שֶׁמָּא לֹא לָמַדְתָּ.
עֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שַׁחֲרִית
מַעֲמִידִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָח
וּמַעֲבִירִין לְפָנָיו פָּרִים וְאֵילִים וּכְבָשִׂים
כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא מַכִּיר וְרָגִיל בָּעֲבוֹדָה.


3 And elders of the court would be sent to him
and would read him the Order of the Day,
and they would say, “My honored High Priest, you read this out,
in case you have forgotten,
in case you have not learned.”
On the eve of the Day of Atonement in the morning,
they would stand him at the Eastern Gate
and pass bulls and rams and sheep before him –
so that he would learn to know them well
and be accustomed to the Service.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:4)


כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים
לֹא הָיוּ מוֹנְעִין מִמֶּנּוּ מַאֲכָל וּמִשְׁתֶּה.
עֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים עִם חֲשֵׁכָה
לֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִים אוֹתוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל הַרְבֵּה
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַמַּאֲכָל מֵבִיא אֶת הַשֵּׁנָה.


4 All the seven days beforehand
they would not limit his food or drink;
but on the eve of the Day of Atonement, before dark fell,
they would not let him eat much,
because food brings on sleep.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:5)


מְסָרוּהוּ זִקְנֵי בֵית דִּין לְזִקְנֵי כְהֻנָּה
וְהֶעֱלוּהוּ לַעֲלִיַּת בֵּית אַבְטִינָס
וְהִשְׁבִּיעוּהוּ, וְנִפְטְרוּ וְהָלְכוּ לָהֶם.
וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
אָנוּ שְׁלוּחֵי בֵית דִּין
וְאַתָּה שְׁלוּחֵנוּ וּשְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין;
מַשְׁבִּיעִין אָנוּ עָלֶיךָ בְּמִי שֶׁשִּׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ בַבַּיִת הַזֶּה
שֶׁלֹּא תְשַׁנֶּה דָבָר מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמַרְנוּ לָךְ.
הוּא פוֹרֵשׁ וּבוֹכֶה
וְהֵן פּוֹרְשִׁין וּבוֹכִין.


5 The elders of the court would bring him to the elders of the
priesthood,
who would take him up to the Avtinas Upper Chamber
and have him take his oath,
and then would part from him and leave.
This is what they would say:
“My honored High Priest, we are the emissaries of the court
and you are our emissary and an emissary of the court;
we have you swear
by the One who has made His name dwell in this House,
that you will not depart in any detail from what we have
taught you.”
And he would turn away and weep,
and they would turn away and weep.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:6)


אִם הָיָה חָכָם – דּוֹרֵשׁ
וְאִם לָאו – תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דּוֹרְשִׁין לְפָנָיו;
וְאִם רָגִיל לִקְרוֹת – קוֹרֵא
וְאִם לָאו – קוֹרִין לְפָנָיו.
וּבַמֶּה קוֹרִין לְפָנָיו?
בְּאִיּוֹב וּבְעֶזְרָא וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים.
זְכַרְיָה בֶּן קְבוּטָל אוֹמֵר:
פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה קָרִיתִי לְפָנָיו בְּדָנִיֵּאל.


6 Then, if he were a scholar, he would interpret Torah;
if not, then scholars would interpret it for him.
If he were accustomed to reading, he would read;
if not, then they would read to him.
What would they read to him?
They read from Job
and from Ezra
and from the books of Chronicles.
Zekharya ben Kevutal says:
I read to him many times
from the book of Daniel.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:7)


בִּקֵּשׁ לְהִתְנַמְנֵם
פִּרְחֵי כְהֻנָּה מַכִּין לְפָנָיו בְּאֶצְבַּע צְרָדָה
וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ:
אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, עֲמֹד וְהָפֵג אַחַת עַל הָרִצְפָּה!
וּמַעֲסִיקִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטַָה.


7 If he began to fall asleep,
then young priests would snap their fingers before him;
they would say,
“My honored High Priest, rise up, banish sleep, once and for all, against the floor.”
And they would keep him occupied
until the time of the slaughtering arrived.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/1:8)


בְּכָל יוֹם
תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ בִּקְרִיאַת הַגֶּבֶר אוֹ סָמוּךְ לוֹ
בֵּין לְפָנָיו בֵּין לְאַחֲרָיו;
בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מֵחֲצוֹת,
וּבָרְגָלִים מֵאַשְׁמוּרָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה;
וְלֹא הָיְתָה קְרִיאַת הַגֶּבֶר מַגַּעַת
עַד שֶׁהָיְתָה הָעֲזָרָה מְלֵאָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.


8 On all other days,
the ashes on the altar were taken up at cock’s crow or thereabouts,
a little before or after;
but on the Day of Atonement
they were taken up at midnight –
and on Festivals,
at the first watch –
and by the time the cock would crow,
the courtyard would be crowded with [the people of] Israel.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:1)


בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה
כָּל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִתְרוֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, תּוֹרֵם;
וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מְרֻבִּין, רָצִין וְעוֹלִין בַּכֶּבֶשׁ
וְכָל הַקּוֹדֵם אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ בְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת – זָכָה.
וְאִם הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִין
הַמְמֻנֶּה אוֹמֵר לָהֶם: הַצְבִּיעוּ;
וּמָה הֵן מוֹצִיאִין?
אַחַת אוֹ שְׁתַּיִם
וְאֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֲגֻדָּל בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ.


1 At first, whoever wished to take up the ashes on the altar
would take them;
and when there were several [priests] who wished to,
they would run up the ramp of the altar,
and the one who was first to reach the upper four cubits,
gained the privilege.
If two of them [ran] alike,
the one who gave their appointment would say:
“Put out fingers!”
And what would they hold out?
Any one finger or two;
but one does not hold out a thumb in the Temple.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:2)


מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִין וְרָצִין וְעוֹלִין בַּכֶּבֶשׁ
וְדָחַף אֶחָד מֵהֶן אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ
וְנָפַל וְנִשְׁבְּרָה רַגְלוֹ.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁרָאוּ בֵית דִּין שֶׁבָּאִין לִידֵי סַכָּנָה
הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ תוֹרְמִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֶלָּא בַפַּיִס.
אַרְבָּעָה פְיָסוֹת הָיוּ שָׁם
וְזֶה הַפַּיִס הָרִאשׁוֹן.


2 Once, two were alike
and when they had run up the ramp of the altar
one pushed the other and he fell,
and his leg was broken.
When the court saw that they were coming into danger,
they instituted that taking up the ashes on the altar
would only be assigned by lots.
Four sets of lots were cast,
and this was the first.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:3)


הַפַּיִס הַשֵּׁנִי
מִי שׁוֹחֵט
מִי זוֹרֵק
מִי מְדַשֵּׁן מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי
וּמִי מְדַשֵּׁן אֶת הַמְּנוֹרָה
וּמִי מַעֲלֶה אֵבָרִים לַכֶּבֶשׁ:
הָרֹאשׁ וְהָרֶגֶל
וּשְׁתֵּי הַיָּדַיִם
הָעֹקֶץ וְהָרֶגֶל
הֶחָזֶה וְהַגֵּרָה
וּשְׁתֵּי הַדְּפָנוֹת
וְהַקְּרָבַיִם
וְהַסֹּלֶת
וְהַחֲבִתִּין
וְהַיַּיִן.
שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר כֹּהֲנִים זָכוּ בוֹ.
אָמַר בֶּן עַזַַּאי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
דֶּרֶךְ הִלּוּכוֹ הָיָה קָרֵב.


3 The second set of lots:
who was to slaughter the daily offering,
who was to throw its blood,
who was to clear the ashes from the Inner Altar,
who was to clear the ashes from the Menora,
and who was to place the limbs of the offering on the ramp of the altar:
the head and right hind leg;
the two forelegs;
the rump and the left hind leg;
the breast and the neck;
the two sides;
the intestines;
the meal;
the pan cakes;
and the wine.
Thirteen priests were given these privileges.
Ben Azai said before Rabbi Akiva, in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
They would offer up the [parts of the] sheep
in the order in which it walked while alive.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:4)


הַפַּיִס הַשְּׁלִישִׁי
חֲדָשִׁים לַקְּטֹרֶת בּוֹאוּ וְהָפִיסוּ.
וְהָרְבִיעִי
חֲדָשִׁים עִם יְשָׁנִים
מִי מַעֲלֶה אֵבָרִים מִן הַכֶּבֶשׁ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ.


4 The third set of lots:
“New priests to the incense,
come and cast lots!”
And the fourth:
New priests and experienced,
who will lift the organs from the ramp onto the altar.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:5)


תָּמִיד קָרֵב בְּתִשְׁעָה, בַּעֲשָׂרָה, בְּאַחַד עָשָׂר, בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר
לֹא פָחוּת וְלֹא יוֹתֵר.
כֵּיצַד?
עַצְמוֹ בְּתִשְׁעָה
בֶּחָג – בְּיַד אֶחָד צְלוֹחִית שֶׁלַּמַּיִם
הֲרֵי כָאן עֲשָׂרָה;
בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם – בְּאַחַד עָשָׂר:
הוּא עַצְמוֹ בְּתִשְׁעָה
וּשְׁנַיִם בְּיָדָם שְׁנֵי גִזְרֵי עֵצִים;
וּבַשַּׁבָּת – בְּאַחַד עָשָׂר:
הוּא עַצְמוֹ בְּתִשְׁעָה
וּשְׁנַיִם בְּיָדָם שְׁנֵי בָזִכֵּי לְבוֹנָה שֶׁלְּלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים;
וּבַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הֶחָג
בְּיַד אֶחָד צְלוֹחִית שֶׁלַּמַּיִם.


5 The daily sacrifice is offered up
by nine, by ten, by eleven and by twelve –
never by less or by more.
How so?
[The offering] itself by nine,
and on Sukkot, one man holds a bowl of water;
this, then, makes ten.
The afternoon sacrifice is offered by eleven:
[the offering] itself by nine,
and two men carry kindling wood.
On Shabbat, by eleven:
[the offering] itself by nine,
and two men carry censers of incense for the showbread.
And on the Shabbat of Sukkot –
one man holds a bowl of water.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:6)


אַיִל קָרֵב בְּאַחַד עָשָׂר:
הַבָּשָׂר – בַּחֲמִשָּׁה
הַקְּרָבַיִם וְהַסֹּלֶת וְהַיַּיִן – בִּשְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם.


6 A ram is offered up by eleven:
the meat by five,
the intestines and the meal and the wine – each by two.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/2:7)


פַּר קָרֵב בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה:
הָרֹאשׁ וְהָרֶגֶל – הָרֹאשׁ בְּאֶחָד, וְהָרֶגֶל בִּשְׁנַיִם
הָעֹקֶץ וְהָרֶגֶל – הָעֹקֶץ בִּשְׁנַיִם, וְהָרֶגֶל בִּשְׁנַיִם
הֶחָזֶה וְהַגֵּרָה – הֶחָזֶה בְּאֶחָד, וְהַגֵּרָה בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
שְׁתֵּי הַיָּדַיִם בִּשְׁנַיִם
שְׁתֵּי הַדְּפָנוֹת בִּשְׁנַיִם
הַקְּרָבַיִם וְהַסֹּלֶת וְהַיַּיִן – בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה שְׁלֹשָׁה.
בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר.
אֲבָל בְּקָרְבַּן הַיָּחִיד
אִם רָצָה לְהַקְרִיב – מַקְרִיב.
הֶפְשֵׁטָן וְנִתּוּחָן שֶׁלָּאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ שָׁוִין.


7 A bull is offered up by twenty-four:
the head and the right hind leg –
the head by one, the leg by two;
the rump and the left hind leg –
the rump by two and the leg by two;
the breast and neck –
the breast by one, the neck by three;
the two forelegs by two;
the two sides by two;
the intestines and the meal and the wine –
each by three.
When is this the case?
For communal offerings.
In the case of individual offerings,
if one priest wishes to offer up [everything], he does.
With regard to their flaying and carving, however,
the two kinds of offering are alike.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:1)


אָמַר לָהֶם הַמְמֻנֶּה:
צְאוּ וּרְאוּ, אִם הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטָה.
אִם הִגִּיעַ
הָרוֹאֶה אוֹמֵר: בַּרְקַאי!
מַתִּתְיָא בֶּן שְׁמוּאֵל אוֹמֵר:
הֵאִיר פְּנֵי כָל הַמִּזְרָח עַד שֶׁבְּחֶבְרוֹן?
וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: הֵן.


1 The appointed [priest] would say,
“Go out and see if the time for slaughtering has come.”
If it had come, the one who saw it would say,
“Light!”
Mattitya ben Shmuel would say,
“Has all the eastern horizon lit up as far as Hebron?”
and the other would answer him “Yes!”


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:2)


וְלָמָּה הֻצְרְכוּ לְכָךְ?
שֶׁפַּעַם אַחַת עָלָה מְאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה
וְדִמּוּ שֶׁהֵאִיר הַמִּזְרָח
וְשָׁחֲטוּ אֶת הַתָּמִיד
וְהוֹצִיאוּהוּ לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה.
הוֹרִידוּ כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל לְבֵית הַטְּבִילָה.
זֶה הַכְּלָל הָיָה בַמִּקְדָּשׁ:
כָּל הַמֵּסִיךְ אֶת רַגְלָיו
טָעוּן טְבִילָה
וְכָל הַמַּטִּיל מַיִם
טָעוּן קִדּוּשׁ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם.


2 Why was this found necessary?
For once the light of the moon came up
and it looked as if the east were alight,
and they slaughtered the daily sacrifice
and had to take it out to the place of burning.
They would take the High Priest down to the ritual bath.
This was the rule in the Temple:
one who sits to relieve himself
requires immersion,
and one who passes water
requires sanctification of the hands and feet.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:3)


אֵין אָדָם נִכְנָס לָעֲזָרָה לָעֲבוֹדָה
אֲפִלּוּ טָהוֹר
עַד שֶׁיִּטְבֹּל.
חָמֵשׁ טְבִילוֹת וַעֲשָׂרָה קִדּוּשִׁין
טוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַיּוֹם
וְכֻלָּן בַּקֹּדֶשׁ עַל בֵּית הַפַּרְוָה
חוּץ מִזּוֹ בִלְבַד.


3 But no one enters the courtyard for service,
even if he is pure,
until he has immersed himself.
On that day the High Priest
would immerse himself five times
and sanctify himself ten times.
And each of these purifications were performed in the Holy Place,
above the Parva Chamber,
except for this one.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:4)


פֵּרְסוּ סָדִין שֶׁלְּבוּץ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הָעָם.
פָּשַׁט יָרַד וְטָבַל, עָלָה וְנִסְתַּפַּג.
הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ בִגְדֵי זָהָב
וְלָבַשׁ וְקִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו.
הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַתָּמִיד.
קְרָצוֹ, וּמֵרֵק אַחֵר שְׁחִיטָה עַל יָדוֹ
קִבֵּל אֶת הַדָּם וּזְרָקוֹ.
נִכְנַס לְהַקְטִיר קְטֹרֶת שֶׁלַּשַּׁחַר
וּלְהֵטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת
וּלְהַקְרִיב אֶת הָרֹאשׁ וְאֶת הָאֵבָרִים
וְאֶת הַחֲבִתִּין וְאֶת הַיַּיִן.


4 A sheet of linen would be stretched out between him and the people.
And he would undress and go down and immerse himself,
come up and dry himself.
They would bring him [his] golden vestments,
and he would dress and sanctify his hands and feet.
Then they would bring him the daily offering.
He would make the first cut,
and another priest would complete the slaughtering;
he would receive the blood and throw it.
And he would enter [the Sanctuary] to burn the morning incense,
and tend the lamps.
And he would offer up the head and the organs,
the pan cakes and the wine.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:5)


קְטֹרֶת שֶׁלַּשַּׁחַר
הָיְתָה קְרֵבָה בֵּין הַדָּם לָאֵבָרִים
שֶׁלְּבֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם
בֵּין אֵבָרִים לַנְּסָכִים.
אִם הָיָה כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל זָקֵן אוֹ אִסְטְנִיס
מְחַמִּין לוֹ חַמִּין
וּמַטִּילִין לְתוֹךְ הַצּוֹנִין
כְּדֵי שֶׁתָּפוּג צִנָּתָן.


5 The morning incense was offered
between [throwing the] blood and [offering the] organs.
That of the afternoon –
between the organs and the libations.
If the High Priest were elderly or delicate,
they would heat water and pour it into the cold,
so that the chill would pass off it.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/3:6)


הֱבִיאוּהוּ לְבֵית הַפַּרְוָה
וּבַקֹּדֶשׁ הָיָתָה.
פֵּרְסוּ סָדִין שֶׁלְּבוּץ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הָעָם.
קִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו, וּפָשַׁט.
רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר:
פָּשַׁט, קִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו.
יָרַד וְטָבַל, עָלָה וְנִסְתַּפַּג.
הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ בִגְדֵי לָבָן
לָבַשׁ וְקִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו.


6 They would bring him to the Parva chamber;
this was in the Holy Place.
A sheet of linen would be stretched out between him and the people,
and he would sanctify his hands and feet, and undress.
Rabbi Meir says,
he would undress and then sanctify his hands and feet.
He would go down and immerse himself,
come up and dry himself.
They would bring him white vestments,
and he would dress and sanctify his hands and feet.

בַּשַּׁחַר
הָיָה לוֹבֵשׁ פְּלוּסִין שֶׁלִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה
וּבֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם
הִנְדְּוִין שֶׁלִּשְׁמוֹנֶה מֵאוֹת זוּז
דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים:
בַּשַּׁחַר הָיָה לוֹבֵשׁ שֶׁלִּשְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר מָנֶה
וּבֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם שֶׁלִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה
הַכֹּל שְׁלֹשִׁים מָנֶה.
אֵלּוּ מִשֶּׁלַּצִּבּוּר
וְאִם רָצָה לְהוֹסִיף, מוֹסִיף מִשֶּׁלּוֹ.


7 In the morning he would wear Pelusium linen
worth twelve manehs,
and in the afternoon, Indian linen
worth eight hundred zuz:
thus says Rabbi Meir.
The sages say:
In the morning he would wear vestments
worth eighteen manehs,
and in the afternoon,
worth twelve manehs –
thirty manehs altogether.
This is what the public provided –
and if he wished to add on to this,
he would add from his own pocket.

בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל פָּרוֹ
וּפָרוֹ הָיָה עוֹמֵד בֵּין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ
רֹאשׁוֹ לַדָּרוֹם וּפָנָיו לַמַּעֲרָב
וְהַכֹּהֵן עוֹמֵד בַּמִּזְרָח וּפָנָיו לַמַּעֲרָב
וְסוֹמֵךְ שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו עָלָיו וּמִתְוַדֶּה.
וְכָךְ הָיָה אוֹמֵר:
אָנָּא הַשֵּׁם
עָוִיתִי, פָּשַׁעְתִּי, חָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ
אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי.
אָנָּא הַשֵּׁם
כַּפֶּר נָא לָעֲוֹנוֹת וְלַפְּשָׁעִים וְלַחֲטָאִים
שֶׁעָוִיתִי וְשֶׁפָּשַׁעְתִּי וְשֶׁחָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ
אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי
כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה עַבְדֶּךָ:
כִּי־בַיּוֹם הַזֶּה יְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיכֶם: וגו׳.
וְהֵן עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו:
׳בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד׳.


8 He would come to his bull;
the bull would be standing between the Antechamber and the altar,
its head to the south, its face turned to the west;
the priest stood to its eastern side
facing west,
and he would press his two hands down upon the bull and confess.
And this is what he would say:
“Please, [LORD] –
I have done wrong,
I have rebelled,
I have sinned before You –
I and my family.
Please, by the Name,
make atonement, please,
for the wrongs
and the rebellions
and sins
that I have done wrong,
I have rebelled,
that I have sinned before You –
I and my family,
as it is written in the Torah of Moses Your servant,
“For you will be atoned on this day…”
And they would respond,
“Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and
all time.”

הַסְּגַן מִימִינוֹ וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ.
וְשָׁם שְׁנֵי שְׂעִירִים
וְקַלְפִּי הָיְתָה שָׁם

שֶׁלְּאֶשְׁכְּרוֹעַ הָיוּ
וַעֲשָׂאָן בֶּן גַּמְלָא שֶׁלְּזָהָב

9 He would come to the eastern part of the courtyard,
north of the altar,
with the Deputy High Priest to his right
and the Head of the [officiating] house to his left.
And there two goats would be standing,
and a ballot would be there,
and in it there would be two lots.
These were made of boxwood,
but Ben Gamla made them out of gold,
and he was spoken of afterwards in praise.

בֶּן קָטִין עָשָׂה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר דַּד לַכִּיּוֹר
שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ אֶלָּא שְׁנַיִם;
וְאַף הוּא עָשָׂה מוּכְנִי לַכִּיּוֹר
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ מֵימָיו נִפְסָלִין בְּלִינָה.
מֻנְבַּז הַמֶּלֶךְ
הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה כָּל יְדוֹת הַכֵּלִים שֶׁלְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁלְּזָהָב
הִילְנִי אִמּוֹ
עָשְׂתָה נִבְרֶשֶׁת שֶׁלַּזָּהָב עַל פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁלַּהֵיכָל;
וְאַף הִיא עָשְׂתָה טַבְלָא שֶׁלַּזָּהָב
שֶׁפָּרָשַׁת סוֹטָה כְתוּבָה עָלֶיהָ.
נִיקָנוֹר
נַעֲשׂוּ נִסִּים לְדַלְתוֹתָיו
וְהָיוּ מַזְכִּירִין אוֹתוֹ לִשְׁבָח.


10 Ben Katin made twelve taps for the basin,
which had not had more than two;
he also made a pulley for the basin,
so that its waters would not become invalid by standing overnight.
King Monobaz
made the handles of all the vessels of the Day of Atonement of gold.
His mother Helene
made a lamp of gold for the opening of the Sanctuary;
she also made a tablet of gold,
with the Sota declaration written on it.
Miracles happened for the doors of Nikanor,
and he was spoken of afterwards in praise.

וְאֵלּוּ לִגְנַאי:
שֶׁלְּבֵית גַּרְמוּ
לֹא רָצוּ לְלַמֵּד עַל מַעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
שֶׁלְּבֵית אַבְטִינָס
לֹא רָצוּ לְלַמֵּד עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הַקְּטֹרֶת
הֻגְרַס בֶּן לֵוִי
הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ פֶּרֶק בַּשִּׁיר
וְלֹא רָצָה לְלַמֵּד
בֶּן קַמְצָר
לֹא רָצָה לְלַמֵּד עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הַכְּתָב.
עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנִים נֶאֱמַר:
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
וְעַל אֵלּוּ נֶאֱמַר:
וְשֵׁם רְשָׁעִים יִרְקָב:


11 And these were spoken of for shame:
Those of the house of Garmu
chose not to teach others the art of the showbread.
Those of the house of Avtinas
chose not to teach others the art of the incense.
Hugras ben Levi knew a lesson in the art of song
and chose not to teach it to others.
Ben Kamtzar
chose not to teach others the art of penmanship.
Of those mentioned first it is said,
“A righteous man’s memory is a blessing…”
and of the others,
“…and the name of the wicked will rot.”


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 4:1

טָרַף בַּקַּלְפִּי
וְהֶעֱלָה שְׁנֵי גוֹרָלוֹת.
אֶחָד כָּתוּב עָלָיו: לַשֵּׁם
וְאֶחָד כָּתוּב עָלָיו: לַעֲזָאזֵל.
הַסְּגַן מִימִינוֹ, וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ.
אִם שֶׁלַּשֵּׁם עָלָה בִימִינוֹ
הַסְּגַן אוֹמֵר לוֹ:
אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, הַגְבַּהּ יְמִינְךָ!
וְאִם שֶׁלַּשֵּׁם עָלָה בִשְׂמֹאלוֹ
רֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב אוֹמֵר לוֹ:
אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, הַגְבַּהּ שְׂמֹאלְךָ!
נְתָנָן עַל שְׁנֵי הַשְּׂעִירִים
וְאוֹמֵר: ׳לַה׳ חַטָּאת׳.
רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר:
לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר ׳חַטָּאת׳
אֶלָּא ׳לַה׳׳.
וְהֵן עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו:
׳בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד׳.


1 The High Priest shook the box,
and drew out each of the two lots.
One of them had written on it “To [the LORD]”;
and the other, “To Azazel.”
The Prefect of the priests would be standing to his right,
and the Head of the ministering house to his left.
If the lot to [the LORD] came up in his right hand,
the Prefect would say to him,
“My honored High Priest, raise your right hand!”
And if the lot to [the LORD] came up in his left hand,
the Head of the ministering house would say,
“My honored High Priest, raise your left!”
He would place the lots upon the two goats and say,
“A sin-offering to [the LORD].”
Rabbi Yishmael says:
There was no need to say “a sin-offering” –
only “to [the LORD].”
And they would respond,
“Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and
all time.”


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 4:2

קָשַׁר לָשׁוֹן שֶׁלִּזְהוֹרִית בְּרֹאשׁ שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית שִׁלּוּחוֹ
וְלַנִּשְׁחָט
כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית שְׁחִיטָתוֹ.
בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל פָּרוֹ שְׁנִיָּה
וְסוֹמֵךְ שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו עָלָיו
וּמִתְוַדֶּה.
וְכָךְ הָיָה אוֹמֵר:
אָנָּא הַשֵּׁם
עָוִיתִי פָּשַׁעְתִּי חָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ
אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי וּבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן עַם קְדוֹשֶׁךָ.
אָנָּא הַשֵּׁם
כַּפֶּר נָא לָעֲוֹנוֹת וְלַפְּשָׁעִים וְלַחֲטָאִים
שֶׁעָוִיתִי וְשֶׁפָּשַׁעְתִּי וְשֶׁחָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ
אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי וּבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן עַם קְדוֹשֶׁךָ
כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה עַבְדֶּךָ:
כִּי־בַיּוֹם הַזֶּה יְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיכֶם לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם
מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם, לִפְנֵי ה׳ תִּטְהָרוּ:
וְהֵן עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו:
׳בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד׳.


2 He would tie a strip of scarlet wool
to the head of the goat that was to be sent away,
and stand it by the place from which it would be sent.
And to the one which would be slaughtered
[he would tie one] at the place where it would be slaughtered.
The High Priest would come to his bull a second time,
and would press his two hands down upon it and confess.
And this is what he would say:
Please, [LORD],
I have done wrong,
I have rebelled,
I have sinned before You –
I and my family
and the descendants of Aaron, Your holy people.
Please, [LORD],
make atonement, please, for the wrongs
and the rebellions
and sins
that I have done wrong,
I have rebelled,
that I have sinned before You –
I and my family
and the descendants of Aaron, Your holy people.
As it is written in the Torah of Moses Your servant,
“For you will be atoned on this day…”
And they would respond,
“Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever.”


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/4:3)


שְׁחָטוֹ
וְקִבֵּל בַּמִּזְרָק אֶת דָּמוֹ
וּנְתָנוֹ לְמִי שֶׁהוּא מְמָרֵס בּוֹ
עַל הָרוֹבֵד הָרְבִיעִי שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל
כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִקְרַשׁ.
נָטַל אֶת הַמַּחְתָּה
וְעָלָה לְרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
וּפִנָּה גֶחָלִים אֵילָךְ וְאֵילָךְ
וְחוֹתֶה מִן הַמְעֻכָּלוֹת הַפְּנִימִיּוֹת
וְיָרַד
וְהִנִּיחָהּ עַל הָרוֹבֵד הָרְבִיעִי שֶׁבָּעֲזָרָה.


3 He would slaughter it
and gather its blood in a bowl,
and give it to the one who would keep it stirring
on the fourth tile of the Sanctuary,
so that it would not congeal.
He would take the coal pan
and go up to the head of the altar,
and clear the spent coals this way and that,
and lift out the inner, live ones,
and then go down and lay the pan on the fourth tile of the courtyard.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/4:4)


בְּכָל יוֹם
הָיָה חוֹתֶה בְשֶׁלַּכֶּסֶף
וּמְעָרֶה בְתוֹךְ שֶׁלַּזָּהָב
וְהַיּוֹם
חוֹתֶה בְשֶׁלַּזָּהָב
וּבָהּ הָיָה מַכְנִיס.
בְּכָל יוֹם
חוֹתֶה בְשֶׁלְּאַרְבַּעַת קַבִּין
וּמְעָרֶה בְתוֹךְ שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת קַבִּין
וְהַיּוֹם
חוֹתֶה בְשֶׁלִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת קַבִּין
וּבָהּ הָיָה מַכְנִיס.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:
בְּכָל יוֹם חוֹתֶה בְשֶׁלִּסְאָה
וּמְעָרֶה בְתוֹךְ שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת קַבִּין;
וְהַיּוֹם חוֹתֶה בְשֶׁלִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת קַבִּין
וּבָהּ הָיָה מַכְנִיס.
בְּכָל יוֹם הָיְתָה כְבֵדָה
וְהַיּוֹם קַלָּה.
בְּכָל יוֹם הָיְתָה יָדָהּ קְצָרָה
וְהַיּוֹם אֲרֻכָּה.
בְּכָל יוֹם הָיָה זְהָבָהּ יָרֹק
וְהַיּוֹם אָדֹם
דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מְנַחֵם.
בְּכָל יוֹם
מַקְרִיב פְּרַס בַּשַּׁחֲרִית וּפְרַס בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם
וְהַיּוֹם
מוֹסִיף מְלֹא חָפְנָיו.
בְּכָל יוֹם הָיְתָה דַקָּה
וְהַיּוֹם דַּקָּה מִן הַדַּקָּה.


4 On all other days,
he would lift out the coals with a silver pan
and empty them into a golden one.
But today he would lift them out with a golden pan,
and with that pan he would bring the coals in.
On all other days
he would lift them with a pan of four kabs
and empty the coals into one of three kabs.
But today
he would lift them with a pan of three kabs,
and with that pan he would bring the coals in.
Rabbi Yose says:
On all other days he would lift them with a pan of a se’ah
and empty the coals into one of three kabs;
but today he would lift them with a pan of three kabs,
and with that pan he would bring the coals in.
On all other days it would be heavy,
but today it was light.
On all other days its handle would be short,
but today it was long.
On all other days would be of yellow gold,
but today of red gold;
thus says Rabbi Menaḥem.
On all other days he would offer up half a maneh in the morning
and half a maneh in the evening,
but today he would add a handful of incense.
On all other days it would be fine –
but today it was finer than fine.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/4:5)


בְּכָל יוֹם
כֹּהֲנִים עוֹלִין בְּמִזְרָחוֹ שֶׁלַּכֶּבֶשׁ
וְיוֹרְדִין בְּמַעֲרָבוֹ
וְהַיּוֹם
כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה בָאֶמְצַע וְיוֹרֵד בָּאֶמְצַע.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
לְעוֹלָם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה בָאֶמְצַע וְיוֹרֵד בָּאֶמְצַע.
בְּכָל יוֹם
כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו מִן הַכִּיּוֹר
וְהַיּוֹם
מִן הַקִּיתּוֹן שֶׁלַּזָּהָב.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
לְעוֹלָם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו מִן הַקִּיתּוֹן שֶׁלַּזָּהָב.


5 On all other days the priests would ascend the eastern side of the ramp to the altar,
and descend at the western side.
But today the High Priest would ascend its center
and descend at its center.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The High Priest would always ascend its center
and descend at its center.
On all other days the High Priest would sanctify his hands and feet from the basin,
but today he would use the golden jug.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The High Priest would always sanctify his hands and feet
using the golden jug.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/4:6)


בְּכָל יוֹם הָיוּ שָׁם אַרְבַּע מַעֲרָכוֹת
וְהַיּוֹם חָמֵשׁ;
דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:
בְּכָל יוֹם שָׁלֹשׁ
וְהַיּוֹם אַרְבַּע.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
בְּכָל יוֹם שְׁתַּיִם
וְהַיּוֹם שָׁלֹשׁ.


6 On all other days,
four fires would be prepared there.
But today there were five;
thus says Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yose says:
On all other days there would be three,
but today there were four.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
On all other days there would be two,
and today there were three.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:1)


הוֹצִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַכַּף וְאֶת הַמַּחְתָּה
וְחָפַן מְלֹא חָפְנָיו
וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ הַכַּף:
הַגָּדוֹל לְפִי גָדְלוֹ, וְהַקָּטָן לְפִי קָטְנוֹ;
וְכָךְ הָיְתָה מִדָּתָהּ.
נָטַל אֶת הַמַּחְתָּה בִּימִינוֹ
וְאֶת הַכַּף בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ.
הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בַּהֵיכָל
עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְבֵין שְׁתֵּי הַפָּרֹכוֹת
הַמַּבְדִּילוֹת בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּבֵין קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים
וּבֵינֵיהֶן אַמָּה.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:
לֹא הָיְתָה שָׁם אֶלָּא פָרֹכֶת אַחַת בִּלְבַד
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְהִבְדִּילָה הַפָּרֹכֶת לָכֶם בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ
וּבֵין קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים:
הַחִיצוֹנָה הָיְתָה פְרוּפָה מִן הַדָּרוֹם
וְהַפְּנִימִית מִן הַצָּפוֹן.
מְהַלֵּךְ בֵּינֵיהֶן, עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַצָּפוֹן.
הִגִּיעַ לַצָּפוֹן, הוֹפֵךְ פָּנָיו לַדָּרוֹם
מְהַלֵּךְ לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ עִם הַפָּרֹכֶת
עַד שֶׁהוּא מַגִּיעַ לָאָרוֹן.
הִגִּיעַ לָאָרוֹן
נוֹתֵן אֶת הַמַּחְתָּה בֵּין שְׁנֵי הַבַּדִּים.
צָבַר אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת עַל גַּבֵּי הַגֶּחָלִים
וְנִתְמַלָּא כָּל הַבַּיִת כֻּלּוֹ עָשָׁן.
יָצָא וּבָא לוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ בֵּית כְּנִיסָתוֹ
וּמִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה בַבַּיִת הַחִיצוֹן
וְלֹא הָיָה מַאֲרִיךְ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ
שֶׁלֹּא לְהַבְעִית אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.


1 They would bring him out the censer and the pan [of incense],
and he would fill his hands [with incense]
and place it in the censer –
as much or little as would fill his hands,
large or small.
He would take the coal pan in his right hand
and the censer in his left.
And he would walk across the Sanctuary
until he reached the place between the two curtains
that divide the Holy from the Holy of Holies
There was a cubit between them.
Rabbi Yose says: There was only one curtain there, as is said:
“The curtain shall make a division for you
between the Holy and the Holy of Holies.”
The outer one was [loosely] tied at the southern end,
and the inner one at the northern.
He would walk between the two
until he reached the northern end.
When he reached the north
he would turn his face to the south
and walk with the curtain to his left
until he had come to the Ark.
When he came to the Ark
he would set down the coal pan between its two staves.
He would pile the incense on the coals,
and the whole house would be filled with [its] smoke.
Then he would go out
by way of his entrance
and pray a short prayer, in the outer Sanctuary,
but he would not spend too long in his prayer,
not to terrify the people.

מִשֶּׁנִּטַּל הָאָרוֹן
אֶבֶן הָיְתָה שָׁם מִימוֹת הַנְּבִיאִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
וּשְׁתִיָּה הָיְתָה נִקְרֵאת
גְּבוֹהָה מִן הָאָרֶץ שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת
וְעָלֶיהָ הָיָה נוֹתֵן.


2 After the Ark was taken away –
there was a stone there ever since the days of the early Prophets,
its name was *Shetiya*,
and it rose three fingers high above the earth –
and he would set [the firepan] down upon that.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:3)


נָטַל אֶת הַדָּם מִמִּי שֶׁהָיָה מְמָרֵס בּוֹ
נִכְנַס לִמְקוֹם שֶׁנִּכְנַס
וְעָמַד בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁעָמַד
וְהִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה
וְלֹא הָיָה מִתְכַּוֵּן לְהַזּוֹת לֹא לְמַעְלָה וְלֹא לְמַטָּה
אֶלָּא כְמַצְלִיף.
וְכָךְ הָיָה מוֹנֶה:
אַחַת
אַחַת וְאַחַת
אַחַת וּשְׁתַּיִם
אַחַת וְשָׁלֹשׁ
אַחַת וְאַרְבַּע
אַחַת וְחָמֵשׁ
אַחַת וָשֵׁשׁ
אַחַת וָשֶׁבַע.
יָצָא
וְהִנִּיחוֹ עַל כַּן הַזָּהָב שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל.


3 He would take the blood
from the one who was keeping it stirring,
and enter the place he had entered
and stand in the place where he had stood,
and he would sprinkle of that blood,
once upward and seven times downward,
not aiming to sprinkle either upward or down,
but as if he were administering lashes.
And he would count thus:
One
one and one
one and two
one and three
one and four
one and five
one and six
one and seven.
Then he would go out and lay [the bowl] down
on the golden stand in the Sanctuary.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 5:4

הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַשָּׂעִיר
שְׁחָטוֹ, וְקִבֵּל בַּמִּזְרָק אֶת דָּמוֹ.
נִכְנַס לִמְקוֹם שֶׁנִּכְנַס
וְעָמַד בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁעָמַד
וְהִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה
וְלֹא הָיָה מִתְכַּוֵּן לְהַזּוֹת לֹא לְמַעְלָה וְלֹא לְמַטָּה
אֶלָּא כְמַצְלִיף.
וְכָךְ הָיָה מוֹנֶה:
אַחַת
אַחַת וְאַחַת
אַחַת וּשְׁתַּיִם וְכוּ׳.
יָצָא
וְהִנִּיחוֹ עַל כַּן הַשֵּׁנִי, שֶׁהָיָה בַהֵיכָל.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
לֹא הָיָה שָׁם אֶלָּא כַן אֶחָד בִּלְבַד.
נָטַל דַּם הַפָּר
וְהִנִּיחַ דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר
וְהִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ עַל הַפָּרֹכֶת שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הָאָרוֹן מִבַּחוּץ
אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה
וְלֹא הָיָה מִתְכַּוֵּן וְכוּ׳.
וְכָךְ הָיָה מוֹנֶה, וְכוּ׳.
נָטַל דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר
וְהִנִּיחַ דַּם הַפָּר
וְהִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ עַל הַפָּרֹכֶת שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הָאָרוֹן מִבַּחוּץ
אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה, וְכוּ׳.
עֵרָה דַם הַפָּר לְתוֹךְ דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר
וְנָתַן אֶת הַמָּלֵא בָרֵיקָן.


4 They would bring him the goat,
and he would slaughter it
and receive its blood in a bowl.
He would enter the place he had entered,
and stand in the place where he had stood,
and he would sprinkle of that blood,
once upward and seven times downward,
not aiming to sprinkle either upward or down,
but as if he were administering lashes.
And he would count thus:
One
one and one
one and two [etc.].
Then he would go out and lay [the bowl] down
on the second golden stand in the Sanctuary.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
There was only one stand.
He would take up the blood of the bull,
and lay down the blood of the goat,
and sprinkle of that blood toward the curtain,
at the place behind which the ark stood, on the outside,
once upward and seven times downward,
not aiming [etc.].
And he would count thus: [etc.].
He would take up the blood of the goat
and lay down the blood of the bull,
and sprinkle of that blood toward the curtain,
at the place behind which the ark stood, on the outside,
once upward and seven times downward [etc.].
And then he would pour the blood of the bull
into the blood of the goat
and drain the full bowl back into the empty one.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:5)


וְיָצָא אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֲשֶׁר לִפְנֵי־ה׳:
זֶה מִזְבַּח הַזָּהָב.
הִתְחִיל מְחַטֵּא וְיוֹרֵד.
מֵהֵיכָן הוּא מַתְחִיל?
מִקֶּרֶן מִזְרָחִית־צְפוֹנִית
צְפוֹנִית־מַעֲרָבִית
מַעֲרָבִית־דְּרוֹמִית
דְּרוֹמִית־מִזְרָחִית.
מְקוֹם שֶׁהוּא מַתְחִיל בַּחַטָּאת עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן
מִשָּׁם הָיָה גוֹמֵר עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר:
בִּמְקוֹמוֹ הָיָה עוֹמֵד וּמְחַטֵּא.
וְעַל כֻּלָּן הָיָה נוֹתֵן מִלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה
חוּץ מִזּוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה לְפָנָיו
שֶׁעָלֶיהָ הָיָה נוֹתֵן מִלְמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה.


5 “He shall go out to the altar, which stands in the presence of the LORD”:
This refers to the Golden Altar.
He would begin to purify it, [sprinkling] downward –
where would he begin?
He would begin at the north-eastern corner,
then move to the north-western,
the south-western,
the south-eastern.
In the position where he began sprinkling the sin-offering blood on the Outer Altar,
there he would finish at the Inner Altar.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He would stand in one place and purify it all.
He would sprinkle upward toward each corner,
except for the one in front of him:
there he would [sprinkle] downward.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 5:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:6)


הִזָּה עַל טָהֳרוֹ שֶׁלַּמִּזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים
וּשְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד מַעֲרָבִי שֶׁלְּמִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן
וְשֶׁלְּמִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד דְּרוֹמִי.
אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ
מִתְעָרְבִין בָּאַמָּה וְיוֹצְאִין לְנַחַל קִדְרוֹן
וְנִמְכָּרִין לַגַּנָּנִין לְזֶבֶל
וּמוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן.


6 Then, seven times, he would sprinkle blood onto the clear space on the altar,
and then he would pour out what was left
against the western base of the Outer Altar;
and that of [the offerings on] the Outer Altar
he would pour against the southern base.
These and those would mingle in the duct
and flow out into the Kidron Valley.
They would be sold to smallholders for fertilizer,
and [one who took them without payment]
had trespassed on the sacred.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 5:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/5:7)


כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הָאָמוּר עַל הַסֵּדֶר
אִם הִקְדִּים מַעֲשֶׂה לַחֲבֵרוֹ
לֹא עָשָׂה כְלוּם;
הִקְדִּים דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר לְדַם הַפָּר
יַחֲזֹר וְיַזֶּה מִדַּם הַשָּׂעִיר לְאַחַר דַּם הַפָּר.
וְאִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָמַר אֶת הַמַּתָּנוֹת שֶׁבִּפְנִים, נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
יָבִיא דָּם אַחֵר
וְיַחֲזֹר וְיַזֶּה בַּתְּחִלָּה בִּפְנִים.
וְכֵן בַּהֵיכָל
וְכֵן בְּמִזְבַּח הַזָּהָב
שֶׁכֻּלָּן כַּפָּרָה בִפְנֵי עַצְמָן.
רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים:
מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁפָּסַק, מִשָּׁם הוּא מַתְחִיל.


7 All the service of the Day of Atonement,
stated in its order –
if [the priest] performed one part before the part before –
nothing was achieved.
If he puts the blood of the goat before the blood of the bull
he had to go back and sprinkle of the blood of the goat again
after the blood of the bull.
If the blood were spilled
before he finished sprinkling it in the inner place,
he must bring more blood
and go back to sprinkle from the beginning in the inner place.
So also in the Sanctuary,
and so at the Golden Altar;
each made a separate atonement in itself.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
From the place where he leaves off,
there he starts again.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:1)


שְׁנֵי שְׂעִירֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
מִצְוָתָן שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן שָׁוִין
בְּמַרְאֶה, וּבְקוֹמָה, וּבְדָמִים
וּבִלְקִיחָתָן כְּאֶחָד.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן שָׁוִין, כְּשֵׁרִין.
לָקַח אֶחָד הַיּוֹם וְאֶחָד לְמָחָר, כְּשֵׁרִין.
מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן
אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגְרִיל מֵת
יִקַּח זוּג לַשֵּׁנִי;
וְאִם מִשֶּׁהִגְרִיל מֵת
יָבִיא זוּג אַחֵר וְיַגְרִיל עֲלֵיהֶם בַּתְּחִלָּה
וְיֹאמַר, אִם שֶׁלַּשֵּׁם מֵת:
זֶה שֶׁעָלָה עָלָיו הַגּוֹרָל ׳לַשֵּׁם׳ יִתְקַיֵּם תַּחְתָּיו;
וְאִם שֶׁלַּעֲזָאזֵל מֵת:
זֶה שֶׁעָלָה עָלָיו הַגּוֹרָל ׳לַעֲזָאזֵל׳ יִתְקַיֵּם תַּחְתָּיו.
וְהַשֵּׁנִי יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב
וְיִמָּכֵר, וְיִפְּלוּ דָמָיו לִנְדָבָה
שֶׁאֵין חַטַּאת צִבּוּר מֵתָה.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תָּמוּת.
וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם, יָמוּת הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
מֵת הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ, יִשָּׁפֵךְ הַדָּם.


1 The two goats for the Day of Atonement are to be alike
in appearance,
in height
and in value,
and to be bought together as one.
But if they are not alike,
they are still valid.
If he buys one on one day and the other on the next,
they are valid.
If one of them dies –
if it happens before the drawing of the lots,
[the High Priest] must take a new partner for the other;
and if one dies after the lots have been drawn,
he must bring another pair
and draw lots over them from the beginning.
And he says, if the one to the LORD has died,
“The one whose lot comes up to the LORD shall take its place;”
and if the one to Azazel has died,
“The one whose lot comes up to Azazel shall take its place.”
The other goat is put to pasture until it becomes unfit for sacrifice,
and is sold, and its money is used for a free-will offering;
for a public sin-offering is not left to die.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
It is left to die.
Rabbi Yehuda also says:
If the blood of the one is spilled [before its sprinkling],
the one to be sent away [to Azazel] is left to die;
and if the goat to be sent away dies,
the blood of the other is poured out [without sprinkling].


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:2)


בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
וְסוֹמֵךְ שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו עָלָיו, וּמִתְוַדֶּה.
וְכָךְ הָיָה אוֹמֵר:
אָנָּא הַשֵּׁם
עָווּ פָּשְׁעוּ חָטְאוּ לְפָנֶיךָ
עַמְּךָ בֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל.
אָנָּא בַשֵּׁם
כַּפֶּר נָא לָעֲוֹנוֹת וְלַפְּשָׁעִים וְלַחֲטָאִים
שֶׁעָווּ וְשֶׁפָּשְׁעוּ וְשֶׁחָטְאוּ לְפָנֶיךָ
עַמְּךָ בֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל
כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה עַבְדֶּךָ, לֵאמֹר:
כִּי־בַיּוֹם הַזֶּה יְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיכֶם לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם
מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם, לִפְנֵי ה׳ תִּטְהָרוּ:
וְהַכֹּהֲנִים וְהָעָם הָעוֹמְדִים בָּעֲזָרָה
כְּשֶׁהָיוּ שׁוֹמְעִים שֵׁם הַמְפֹרָשׁ
שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵא מִפִּי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
הָיוּ כוֹרְעִים וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים וְנוֹפְלִים עַל פְּנֵיהֶם
וְאוֹמְרִים: ׳בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד׳.


2 The High Priest would come to the goat that is to be sent away
and press his two hands down upon it and confess.
And this is what he would say:
Please, [LORD],
Your people Israel
have done wrong,
have rebelled,
have sinned before You –
Please, by the Name,
make atonement, please,
for the wrongs
and the rebellions
and sins
that Your people Israel
have done wrong,
have rebelled,
and have sinned before You –
as it is written in the Torah of Moses Your servant,
“For you will be atoned on this day and made pure;
of all your sins before the LORD you shall be purified.”
And the priests and all the people who were standing in the courtyard,
when they heard the Name
spoken out loud by the High Priest,
would bow down in worship;
would fall upon their faces and say –
“Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever.”


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:3)


מְסָרוֹ לְמִי שֶׁהָיָה מוֹלִיכוֹ.
הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לְהוֹלִיכוֹ
אֶלָּא שֶׁעָשׂוּ כֹהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים קְבַע
וְלֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהוֹלִיכוֹ.
אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
מַעֲשֶׂה וְהוֹלִיכוֹ עַרְסְלָא
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה.


3 The goat would be given to the one who would lead it.
Everyone is valid to lead it,
but the High Priests made it their custom
not to allow a lay Israelite to lead it.
Rabbi Yose said:
Once Arsela led it,
and he was of Israel.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:4)


וְכֶבֶשׁ עָשׂוּ לוֹ
מִפְּנֵי הַבַּבְלִיִּים שֶׁהָיוּ מְתַלְּשִׁים בִּשְׂעָרוֹ
וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ:
טֹל וָצֵא, טֹל וָצֵא!
מִיקִירֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם הָיוּ מְלַוִּין אוֹתוֹ עַד סֻכָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה.
עֶשֶׂר סֻכּוֹת מִירוּשָׁלִַם וְעַד צוּק
תִּשְׁעִים רִיס
שִׁבְעָה וּמֶחֱצָה לְכָל מִיל.


4 They built a ramp for these,
because of the Babylonians who used to pull at their hair saying,
“Take it, go on, take it and go!”
The honored of Jerusalem used to accompany him
as far as the first hut;
there were ten huts between Jerusalem and the crag.
It was a distance of ninety riss,
and there are seven and a half riss in a mil.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:5)


עַל כָּל סֻכָּה וְסֻכָּה
אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: הֲרֵי מָזוֹן וַהֲרֵי מַיִם
וּמְלַוִּין אוֹתוֹ מִסֻּכָּה לְסֻכָּה
חוּץ מֵאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבָּהֶן
שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַגִּיעַ עִמּוֹ לַצּוּק
אֶלָּא עוֹמֵד מֵרָחוֹק וְרוֹאֶה אֶת מַעֲשָׂיו.


5 At every hut they would say to him
“Here is food and here is water,”
and they would walk with him from one hut to the next,
except for the last;
[the man in the last hut] would not come with him to the crag,
but would stand at a distance and see what he did.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 6:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:6)


מֶה הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה?
חוֹלֵק לָשׁוֹן שֶׁלִּזְהוֹרִית
חֶצְיוֹ קָשַׁר בַּסֶּלַע
וְחֶצְיוֹ קָשַׁר בֵּין שְׁתֵּי קַרְנָיו
וּדְחָפוֹ לַאֲחוֹרָיו
וְהוּא מִתְגַּלְגֵּל וְיוֹרֵד
וְלֹא הָיָה מַגִּיעַ לַחֲצִי הָהָר, עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אֵבָרִים אֵבָרִים.
בָּא וְיָשַׁב לוֹ תַּחַת סֻכָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה
עַד שֶׁתֶּחְשַׁךְ.
וּמֵאֵימָתַי מְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים?
מִשֶּׁיֵּצֵא חוּץ לְחוֹמַת יְרוּשָׁלִַם.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
מִשָּׁעַת דְּחִיָּתוֹ לַצּוּק.


6 And what would he do?
He would divide the scarlet strip in two,
tie half to the rock and half between the goat’s two horns,
and he would push the goat backwards,
it would roll down and down,
and it would not fall halfway down the mountain
before it was torn limb from limb.
The man would go and sit in the last hut until dark.
And from what moment do his clothes become impure?
From the moment they pass across the wall of Jerusalem.
Rabbi Shimon says:
From the moment it is pushed from the cliff.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 6:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:7)


בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל הַפָּר וְאֵצֶל הַשָּׂעִיר הַנִּשְׂרָפִין.
קְרָעָן
וְהוֹצִיא אֶת אֵמוּרֵיהֶן
נְתָנָן בַּמָּגִיס
וְהִקְטִירָן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
קְלָעָן בַּמִּקְלָעוֹת
וְהוֹצִיאָן לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה.
וּמֵאֵימָתַי מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים?
מִשֶּׁיֵּצְאוּ חוּץ לְחוֹמַת הָעֲזָרָה.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
מִשֶּׁיִּצַּת הָאוּר בְּרֻבָּן.


7 The High Priest would come to the bull and the goat to be burnt.
He would cut them open and take out the sacrificial parts,
place them in a basin
and burn them like incense on the altar.
Then he would braid the limbs together
and send them out to the place of burning.
And from what moment do [the bearers’] clothes become impure?
From the moment they leave the courtyard walls.
Rabbi Shimon says:
From the moment the fire has taken hold of the greater part [of the limbs].


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 6:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/6:8)


אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל:
הִגִּיעַ שָׂעִיר לַמִּדְבָּר.
וּמִנַּיִן הָיוּ יוֹדְעִין שֶׁהִגִּיעַ שָׂעִיר לַמִּדְבָּר?
דַּרְכִּיּוֹת הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין
וּמְנִיפִין בַּסּוּדָרִין
וְיוֹדְעִין שֶׁהִגִּיעַ שָׂעִיר לַמִּדְבָּר.
אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
וַהֲלֹא סִימָן גָּדוֹל הָיָה לָהֶם!
מִירוּשָׁלִַם וְעַד בֵּית חִדּוּדוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה מִילִין;
הוֹלְכִין מִיל
וְחוֹזְרִין מִיל
וְשׁוֹהִין כְּדֵי מִיל
וְיוֹדְעִין שֶׁהִגִּיעַ שָׂעִיר לַמִּדְבָּר.
רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר:
וַהֲלֹא סִימָן אַחֵר הָיָה לָהֶם!
לָשׁוֹן שֶׁלִּזְהוֹרִית הָיָה קָשׁוּר עַל פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁלַּהֵיכָל
וּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ שָׂעִיר לַמִּדְבָּר הָיָה הַלָּשׁוֹן מַלְבִּין
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: אִם־יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים, כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ:


8 They would say to the High Priest,
“The goat has reached the desert.”
How would they know when the goat had reached the desert?
They would form look-out posts,
and wave sheets of cloth
to let them know the goat had reached the desert.
Rabbi Yehuda said:
Was there not a better sign than this!
From Jerusalem to Beit Ḥidudo was three mils.
They would walk a mil,
walk back a mil,
then wait the time it takes to walk a mil,
and know that the goat had reached the desert.
Rabbi Yishmael says:
Was there not another sign as well?
A strip of scarlet wool was tied at the Sanctuary doors,
and when the goat reached the desert, the wool would turn white,
as it is said:
“If Your sins are like scarlet,
they shall be whitened like snow.”


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/7:1)


בָּא לוֹ כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל לִקְרוֹת.
אִם רָצָה לִקְרוֹת בְּבִגְדֵי בוּץ – קוֹרֵא
וְאִם לֹא – קוֹרֵא בְּאִצְטְלִית לָבָן מִשֶּׁלּוֹ.
חַזַּן הַכְּנֶסֶת נוֹטֵל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וְנוֹתְנוֹ לְרֹאשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת
וְרֹאשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת נוֹתְנוֹ לַסְּגַן
וְהַסְּגַן נוֹתְנוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹמֵד וּמְקַבֵּל וְקוֹרֵא (עוֹמֵד, וְקוֹרֵא)
׳אַחֲרֵי מוֹת׳ וְ׳אַךְ בֶּעָשׂוֹר׳.
וְגוֹלֵל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
וּמַנִּיחָהּ בְּחֵיקוֹ
וְאוֹמֵר: יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁקָּרָאתִי לִפְנֵיכֶם כָּתוּב כָּאן.
׳וּבֶעָשׂוֹר׳ שֶׁבְּחוּמַשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים
קוֹרֵא עַל פֶּה.
וּמְבָרֵךְ עָלֶיהָ שְׁמוֹנֶה בְרָכוֹת:
עַל הַתּוֹרָה
וְעַל הָעֲבוֹדָה
וְעַל הַהוֹדָאָה
וְעַל מְחִילַת הֶעָוֹן
וְעַל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
וְעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן
(וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלִַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ)
וְעַל הַכֹּהֲנִים בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן
וְעַל שְׁאָר הַתְּפִלָּה.


1 The High Priest then came to read out from the Scriptures.
If he wished to read wearing linen vestments,
he would read in them,
and if not
he would read wearing his own robe of white.
The Shamash of the synagogue takes the Torah scroll
and gives it to the synagogue leader,
and the leader of the synagogue gives it to the Deputy,
and the Deputy gives it to the High Priest,
and the High Priest stands and receives it and reads
[the passage beginning] “After the death…”
and [the passage beginning] “On the tenth…”
And then he rolls up the scroll
and places it in his breast,
and says,
“More than I have read to you is written here.”
And [the passage beginning] “On the tenth…” from the book of Numbers,
he recites from memory;
over this he makes eight blessings:
for the Torah,
and for the Service
and for Thanksgiving
and for the Forgiveness of Iniquity;
for the Temple its own blessing,
for Israel their own,
(for Jerusalem her own,)
for the Priests their own –
and for all the rest of the prayers.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/7:2)


הָרוֹאֶה כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל כְּשֶׁהוּא קוֹרֵא
אֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה פַּר וְשָׂעִיר הַנִּשְׂרָפִים
וְהָרוֹאֶה פַּר וְשָׂעִיר הַנִּשְׂרָפִים
אֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל כְּשֶׁהוּא קוֹרֵא.
וְלֹא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיְתָה דֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה
וּמְלֶאכֶת שְׁנֵיהֶן שָׁוָה כְאַחַת.


2 One who sees the High Priest as he reads
does not see the bull and the goat being burned,
and one who sees the bull and the goat being burned
does not see the High Priest as he reads.
Not because it is not allowed,
but because the way between is long,
and they happen together, alike as one.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/7:3)


אִם בְּבִגְדֵי בוּץ קוֹרֵא
קִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
פָּשַׁט יָרַד וְטָבַל, עָלָה וְנִסְתַּפַּג.
הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ בִגְדֵי זָהָב
וְלָבַשׁ וְקִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
וְיָצָא וְעָשָׂה אֶת אֵילוֹ וְאֶת אֵיל הָעָם
וְאֶת שִׁבְעַת כְּבָשִׂים תְּמִימִים בְּנֵי שָׁנָה;
דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר:
עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁלַּשַּׁחַר הָיוּ קְרֵבִין.
וּפַר הָעוֹלָה וְשָׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בַחוּץ
הָיוּ קְרֵבִין עִם תָּמִיד שֶׁלְּבֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם.


3 If [the High Priest] read in [the priestly] linen vestments,
he would sanctify his hands and feet,
undress and go down and immerse himself,
come up and dry himself.
They would bring him his golden vestments,
and he would put them on
and sanctify his hands and feet,
and go out and perform the offering of his ram
and of the ram of the people,
and the seven unblemished yearling lambs;
thus says Rabbi Eliezer.
Rabbi Akiva says:
With the regular morning offering
these too would be offered.
The bull of the burnt offering
and the goat, offered outside
would be sacrificed with the daily offering of the afternoon.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/7:4)


קִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
וּפָשַׁט וְיָרַד וְטָבַל וְעָלָה וְנִסְתַּפַּג.
הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ בִגְדֵי לָבָן וְלָבַשׁ
וְקִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלַָיו.
נִכְנַס לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַכַּף וְאֶת הַמַּחְתָּה.
קִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
וּפָשַׁט וְיָרַד וְטָבַל, עָלָה וְנִסְתַּפַּג.
הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ בִגְדֵי זָהָב וְלָבַשׁ
וְקִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
וְנִכְנַס לְהַקְטִיר אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת שֶׁלְּבֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם
וּלְהֵטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת
וְקִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו, וּפָשַׁט.
הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ בִגְדֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְלָבַשׁ.
וּמְלַוִּין אוֹתוֹ עַד בֵּיתוֹ.
וְיוֹם טוֹב הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה לְאוֹהֲבָיו
בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁיָּצָא בְשָׁלוֹם מִן הַקֹּדֶשׁ.


4 [The High Priest] would sanctify his hands and feet,
undress and go down and immerse himself,
come up and dry himself.
They would bring him white vestments
and he would put them on,
and sanctify his hands and feet.
He would enter within
to retrieve the censer and the firepan.
Then he would sanctify his hands and feet,
undress and go down and immerse himself,
come up and dry himself.
They would bring him his golden vestments
and he would put them on,
sanctify his hands and feet,
enter within to burn the incense of the afternoon,
and tend to the lights,
and sanctify his hands and feet
and undress.
Then they would bring him his own clothes,
and he would put them on.
And they would accompany him to his house,
and he would make a celebration for his friends,
when he left the Holy Place in peace.


###### The Koren Yom Kippur Mahzor; Ashkenaz, Yom Kippur Evening, Massekhet Yoma 7:5

כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּשְׁמוֹנָה כֵלִים
וְהַהֶדְיוֹט בְּאַרְבָּעָה:
בִּכְתֹנֶת
וּבְמִכְנְסַיִם
וּבְמִצְנֶפֶת
וּבְאַבְנֵט.
מוֹסִיף עָלָיו כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל:
חֹשֶׁן
וְאֵפוֹד
וּמְעִיל
וָצִיץ.
בְּאֵלּוּ נִשְׁאָלִין בְּאוּרִים וְתֻמִּים;
וְאֵין נִשְׁאָלִין אֶלָּא לַמֶּלֶךְ
וּלְבֵית דִּין
וּלְמִי שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר צָרִיךְ בּוֹ.


5 The High Priest serves wearing eight garments
and the lay priests in four:
in the tunic,
the breeches,
the miter,
and the sash;
along with these the High Priest wears
the breastplate,
the Ephod,
the robe,
and the frontlet.
By means of these [vestments], the Urim and Tumim are enquired of;
but enquired of only for the sake of the king or the Court
or for one to whom the public looks for its need.

בַּאֲכִילָה וּבִשְׁתִיָּה
וּבִרְחִיצָה
וּבְסִיכָה
וּבִנְעִילַת הַסַּנְדָּל

וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין.


1 On the Day of Atonement it is prohibited
to eat or drink,
to wash,
to anoint oneself,
to wear shoes
or to have marital relations.
But a king and a bride may wash their faces,
and a woman after childbirth may wear shoes:
thus says Rabbi Eliezer.
The sages say these too are forbidden.

הָאוֹכֵל כְּכוֹתֶבֶת הַגַּסָּה
כָּמוֹהָ וּכְגַרְעִינָתָהּ
וְהַשּׁוֹתֶה מְלֹא לֻגְמָיו
חַיָּב.
כָּל הָאֹכָלִין מִצְטָרְפִין לְכַכּוֹתֶבֶת
וְכָל הַמַּשְׁקִין מִצְטָרְפִין לִמְלֹא לֻגְמָיו.
הָאוֹכֵל וְהַשּׁוֹתֶה אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין.


2 One who eats something the size of a coarse date with its pit,
or one who drinks his mouth’s full,
is liable.
Any foods he eats count together for the date measure,
and anything he drinks counts together for the mouthful;
but food and drink are not counted with each other.

אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא חַטָּאת אַחַת.
אָכַל וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכָה
חַיָּב שְׁתֵּי חַטָּאוֹת.

3 If one eats and drinks in one oversight,
he is only liable for one sin-offering.
If he eats and does work,
he is liable for two sin-offerings.
If he eats foods that are not fit for eating
or drinks liquids that are not fit for drinking,
or brine, or the juice of pickled fish,
he is not liable.

but one has them practice a year or two years before,
so that they become accustomed to the mitzvot.

חוֹלֶה

5 If a pregnant woman is [overcome] by the smell [of food] –
she is allowed to eat until her spirit returns.
A person who is ill
is fed according to the instructions of experts,
or, if there are no experts there,
then according to his own instructions,

מִי שֶׁאֲחָזוֹ בֻלְמוֹס
מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ אֲפִלּוּ דְבָרִים טְמֵאִים
עַד שֶׁיֵּאוֹרוּ עֵינָיו.
מִי שֶׁנְּשָׁכוֹ כֶלֶב שׁוֹטֶה
אֵין מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ מֵחֲצַר הַכָּבֵד שֶׁלּוֹ
וְרַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ מַתִּיר.
וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ:
הַחוֹשֵׁשׁ בִּגְרוֹנוֹ
מַטִּילִין לוֹ סַם בְּתוֹךְ פִּיו בַּשַּׁבָּת

6 A person overcome with *bulmus*
is fed, even with impure things,
until his vision is restored.
One who has been bitten by a mad dog
is not fed of the appendage of its liver;
Rabbi Matia ben Ḥarash permits this.
Rabbi Matia ben Ḥarash also said this:
If a person has pain in his throat,
one may put medicine into his mouth on Shabbat,
because it may be a life-saving treatment,
and any doubtful case of life and death
is enough to suspend the Shabbat prohibition.

מִי שֶׁנָּפְלָה עָלָיו מַפֹּלֶת
סָפֵק הוּא שָׁם סָפֵק אֵינוֹ שָׁם
סָפֵק חַי סָפֵק מֵת
סָפֵק נָכְרִי סָפֵק יִשְׂרָאֵל
מְפַקְּחִין עָלָיו אֶת הַגַּל.
מְצָאוּהוּ חַי – מְפַקְּחִין עָלָיו
וְאִם מֵת – יַנִּיחוּהוּ.


7 If debris falls on a person,
and it is not clear whether he is still there or not,
or not clear whether he is alive or dead,
or whether he is Jewish or gentile –
one must remove the rocks from him.
If he is found alive,
one removes them from him,
and if he is dead,
one leaves him.

חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם וַדַּאי מְכַפְּרִין
מִיתָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפְּרִין עִם הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
הַתְּשׁוּבָה מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל עֲבֵרוֹת הַקַּלּוֹת
עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
וְעַל הַחֲמוּרוֹת הִיא תוֹלָה
עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וִיכַפֵּר.


8 A sin-offering, and the guilt-offering for a certain sin
make atonement;
death and the Day of Atonement
make atonement where there is repentance.
Repentance makes atonement for small sins,
whether of deed or of omission;
over serious sins, repentance holds [the judgment] over,
until the Day of Atonement comes, and atones.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/8:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/The%20Koren%20Yom%20Kippur%20Mahzor%3B%20Ashkenaz/s/Yom%20Kippur%20Evening,_Massekhet%20Yoma/r/8:9)


הָאוֹמֵר:
אֶחֱטָא וְאָשׁוּב, אֶחֱטָא וְאָשׁוּב
אֵין מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה
אֶחֱטָא, וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר
אֵין יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר.
עֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבֵּין אָדָם לַמָּקוֹם
יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר
עֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבֵּין אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ
אֵין יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר
עַד שֶׁיְּרַצֶּה אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ.
אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי ה׳ תִּטְהָרוּ:
עֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבֵּין אָדָם לַמָּקוֹם
יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר
עֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבֵּין אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ
אֵין יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר, עַד שֶׁיְּרַצֶּה אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ.
אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
אַשְׁרֵיכֶם יִשְׂרָאֵל!
לִפְנֵי מִי אַתֶּם מִטַּהֲרִין?
מִי מְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם?
אֲבִיכֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְזָרַקְתִּי עֲלֵיכֶם מַיִם טְהוֹרִים, וּטְהַרְתֶּם:
וְאוֹמֵר: מִקְוֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳:
מָה הַמִּקְוֶה מְטַהֵר אֶת הַטְּמֵאִים
אַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּך הוּא מְטַהֵר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.


9 One who says
“I shall sin and then repent, I shall sin and then repent” –
he is not given the chance to repent.
If he says “I shall sin and the Day of Atonement will atone” –
the Day of Atonement will not make him atonement.
For sins between a man and his God,
the Day of Atonement makes atonement;
for sins between a man and his fellow,
the Day of Atonement does not make atonement,
until he makes peace with his fellow.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azaria interpreted this verse:
“Of all your *sins before the* *LORD* you shall be purified.”
for sins that are between a man and his God,
the Day of Atonement makes atonement;
for sins between a man and his fellow,
the Day of Atonement does not make atonement,
until he makes peace with his fellow.
Rabbi Akiva said:
Happy are you, Israel:
before whom do you purify yourselves,
and who purifies you –
Your Father in heaven,
as it is said “I shall throw pure waters over you
and you shall be pure.”
And say, “Israel’s hope [*mikveh*] is the LORD” –
as a ritual bath [*mikveh*] makes those who were impure, pure –
so the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies Israel.

אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָֽׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּֽנוּ עַל נְטִילַת יָדָֽיִם.

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם
אֲשֶׁר יָצַר אֶת הָאָדָם בְּחָכְמָה
וּבָרָא בוֹ נְקָבִים נְקָבִים, חֲלוּלִים חֲלוּלִים.
גָּלוּי וְיָדֽוּעַ לִפְנֵי כִסֵּא כְבוֹדֶֽךָ
שֶׁאִם יִפָּתֵֽחַ אֶחָד מֵהֶם אוֹ יִסָּתֵם אֶחָד מֵהֶם
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְקַיֵּם וְלַעֲמֹד לְפָנֶֽיךָ.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, רוֹפֵא כָל בָּשָׂר וּמַפְלִיא לַעֲשׂוֹת.


בָּרוּךְ Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who formed man in wisdom
and created in him many orifices and cavities.
It is revealed and known before the throne of Your glory
that were one of them to be ruptured or blocked,
it would be impossible to survive
and stand before You.
Blessed are You, LORD, Healer of all flesh who does wondrous deeds.

אֱלֹהַי
נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַֽתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה הִיא.
אַתָּה בְרָאתָהּ, אַתָּה יְצַרְתָּהּ, אַתָּה נְפַחְתָּהּ בִּי
וְאַתָּה מְשַׁמְּרָהּ בְּקִרְבִּי, וְאַתָּה עָתִיד לִטְּלָהּ מִמֶּֽנִּי
וּלְהַחֲזִירָהּ בִּי לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא.
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה בְקִרְבִּי, מוֹדֶה/מוֹדָה/ אֲנִי לְפָנֶֽיךָ
יהוה אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי
רִבּוֹן כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים, אֲדוֹן כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, הַמַּחֲזִיר נְשָׁמוֹת לִפְגָרִים מֵתִים.


אֱלֹהַי My God,
the soul You placed within me is pure.
You created it, You formed it, You breathed it into me,
and You guard it while it is within me. One day You will take it from me,
and restore it to me in the time to come.
As long as the soul is within me, I will thank You,
LORD my God and God of my ancestors,
Master of all works, LORD of all souls.
Blessed are You, LORD, who restores souls to lifeless bodies.
